- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.

- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.

name: OpenCode
run-name: "OpenCode #${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}${{ github.event.issue.title && format(' — {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue_number:
        description: Existing issue to run
        required: true
        type: string

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: opencode-issue-${{ github.repository }}-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  prepare:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || (github.event.action == 'opened' && contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'OpenCode'))
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: write
    uses: denaidark/OhMyGithub/.github/workflows/opencode-prepare.yml@3b460fef6b0cbee61ae301726c8a54b00b73bfd2
    with:
      runtime_ref: 3b460fef6b0cbee61ae301726c8a54b00b73bfd2

  opencode:
    needs: prepare
    if: needs.prepare.outputs.approved == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: read
      pull-requests: write
    uses: denaidark/OhMyGithub/.github/workflows/opencode-reusable.yml@3b460fef6b0cbee61ae301726c8a54b00b73bfd2
    with:
      runtime_ref: 3b460fef6b0cbee61ae301726c8a54b00b73bfd2
      issue_number: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.issue_number }}
      request: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.request }}
      issue_title: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.issue_title }}
      labels_json: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.labels_json }}
      sender: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.sender }}
      target_ref: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.target_ref }}
      target_sha: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.target_sha }}
    secrets:
      OPENCODE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENCODE_API_KEY }}
      OPENCODE_AUTH_JSON: ${{ secrets.OPENCODE_AUTH_JSON }}
      AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY: ${{ secrets.AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY }}
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}

I want you to build a first-person shooter at the level of the most recent Call of Duty games. It should be utterly perfect, visually beautiful, with every single thing done at AAA quality—from textures to physics to anything you could think of. Fan out sub-agents and have sub-agents tackle each one individually so that the game is utterly perfect. Have a separate sub-agent check each item visually to ensure it looks triple A. That separate sub-agent should be a really harsh critic, and if it doesn't look triple A, keep iterating until it does. Don't stop until each sub-agent is utterly wowed with the quality when compared with the actual Call of Duty game. It should literally compare them side by side blind and say which one looks better. Do this in ThreeJS. Continue iterating until it's utterly perfect. Fan out sub-agents and ultracode.
# 🤯 OMG — Oh My GitHub ### 🚀 One Prompt In. A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. - 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation. - 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime. - 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes. - 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/` branch. - 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility. - 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue. - 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes. ## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML. ```text model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free skill/load-sketchfab-threejs skill/gauntlet-loop ``` The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. Shared skills are discovered from: ```text .agents/skills//SKILL.md ``` ## 🔄 OpenCode Workflow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Trigger] --> B[Prepare project] B --> C[Run build.md] C --> D[Run verify.md] D --> E{Public app works?} E -- No --> F[Run public-app-fix.md] F --> E E -- Yes --> G[Run completion-report.md] G --> H{Screenshots exist?} H -- No --> I[Run screenshot-evidence.md] I --> H H -- Yes --> J[Commit and push] J --> K[Create immutable project link] K --> L[Publish report] L --> M[Complete] ``` ## 🏗️ Architecture ```text ┌──────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ GitHub issue │ ──▶ │ GitHub Actions │ ──▶ │ OpenCode │ │ + issue text │ │ runner + labels │ │ + .agents │ └──────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └──────┬───────┘ │ ┌─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ Build code Run tests Verify app │ │ │ └─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┘ ▼ ┌────────────────────────┐ │ Commit store + preview │ └────────────────────────┘ ``` ## 🔐 Security and Access - 🔑 You do not need to create or store a project-specific AI API key. - 🖥️ You do not need to operate a dedicated build server. - ☁️ Execution happens in GitHub Actions. - 🔒 Temporary SSH and preview access exists only for the workflow run. - 👀 Review the generated commit before integrating it. - 🛡️ Restrict who can apply the `OpenCode` label in repositories that accept public issues. > “No servers needed” means no servers for you to provision or maintain. The workflow still uses GitHub-hosted Actions infrastructure and temporary workflow services. ## 📁 Project Structure ```text 📦 OMG ├─ .github/workflows/opencode.yml # 🤖 Main issue-to-project workflow ├─ wiki/opencode.md # 📖 Workflow and session notes ├─ wiki/testing.md # 🧪 Verification guidance └─ AGENTS.md # 🧭 Repository instructions ``` ## 🧪 Local Validation Validate the workflow definition before pushing changes: ```sh actionlint .github/workflows/opencode.yml git diff --check ``` ## 🐛 Troubleshooting | Problem | What to check |

content.text:
No "start" button necessary; experience should auto-run. Good.

Now, build quality. Let's think about the visual design deeply.

Concept: "DEA — Goddess of Everything" hyperpop 3D altar. A chrome female deity suspended in a neon void, with orbiting rings, particle galaxy, reflective floor, bloom. User can click powers: CREATE LIFE, DESTROY, CHANGE, EVERYTHING. Each triggers dramatic scene effects with animated visuals and text.

Technical:
- Three.js r16x via vendored module. Need addons: EffectComposer, RenderPass, UnrealBloomPass, OutputPass, OrbitControls? We can implement orbit drag ourselves. For bloom, addons require imports of three from "three" specifier, so import maps needed. We can vendor three module and addons, use importmap mapping "three" -> "./vendor/three.module.js" and "three/addons/" -> "./vendor/addons/". Need to download addons: postprocessing/EffectComposer.js, RenderPass.js, UnrealBloomPass.js, OutputPass.js, ShaderPass.js, MaskPass.js, CopyShader.js, LuminosityHighPassShader.js, OutputShader.js; maybe OrbitControls.js, RoomEnvironment.js? For chrome, environment map from a procedural PMREM scene (RoomEnvironment) gives nice reflections. Alternatively generate gradient env via CanvasTexture + EquirectangularReflectionMapping. PMREM from a procedural room would look better. RoomEnvironment addon exists. Could also create our own env scene with neon planes, then PMREMGenerator.fromScene. That gives hot pink/cyan reflections on chrome — hyperpop.

- Female figure: procedural using lathe geometries for torso, head sphere, limbs capsules, hair as many curves/tubes. Posed gracefully with arms raised. A stylized "goddess" silhouette. Materials: iridescent chrome (MeshPhysicalMaterial metalness 1, roughness 0.15, envMap), plus emissive accents. Need it to read clearly as female: silhouette with waist, hips, bust hint, long hair, maybe a flowing gown/skirt. A gown built with custom geometry with wavy hem, translucent iridescent. Could look ethereal. Add a halo ring, floating crown shards.

Maybe better to use a known 3D model from Sketchfab? The skill is available and designed for this. But licensing, download size, animations... Could search for a goddess statue. But time/complexity and attribution. Procedural can be cohesive and stylized hyperpop, and interactive morphing is easier. I'll go procedural but high quality with careful design.

Figure construction details:
- Scale figure ~3 units tall, centered at y=0 on a reflective disc floor.
- Skin: iridescent white/pink pearl with clearcoat, subtle emissive rim. Actually "female God" — a chrome statue goddess reads iconic. Add glossy black? Hyperpop likes chrome + hot pink.
- Body parts via LatheGeometry profiles:
  - torso profile from hips to shoulders with waist pinch, bust protrusion can't be lathe (radial symmetric) but can add two spheres for chest, scaled subtly, plus a chest plate.
  - hips/pelvis sphere scaled.
  - neck cylinder, head sphere scaled slightly (y 1.15).
  - arms: upper/lower capsules with joint spheres, posed: one arm raised with palm up conjuring a glowing orb, other extended downward/side. Use groups and rotations.
  - legs mostly hidden by a flowing skirt? A goddess gown with slit. Simpler: long legs as tapered cylinders with heeled feet, plus translucent flowing skirt panels around hips.
  - hair: long flowing strands as CatmullRom curves -> TubeGeometry, dark chrome/black with magenta highlights, flowing outward as if zero-g. Crown/halo.
- Face: minimalist, no detailed features; maybe glowing eyes (two small emissive spheres) to give life. Chrome face with two magenta glowing eyes looks striking.

Scene:
- Dark background with radial gradient (canvas texture as scene.background? Use large sphere with shader gradient).
- Reflective floor: MeshStandardMaterial metalness .9 roughness .2 with envmap, plus grid lines glowing pink/cyan fading with distance (custom shader on plane), and circular platform.
- Particles: 3000 points with additive blending, colors pink/cyan/white, drifting.
- Orbiting rings: torus geometries with emissive gradient shader, tilted, rotating.
- Floating shards/crystals around.
- Volumetric-ish god rays? Could add cones with additive transparent material. Bloom handles glow.
- Camera slowly orbits, with mouse parallax; drag to orbit, scroll to zoom (limited). Auto idle drift.
- Post: UnrealBloom strength ~1.1, radius .7, threshold .6; plus custom film grain/chromatic aberration shader? Keep it manageable: add a final ShaderPass with vignette + subtle chromatic aberration + grain + scanlines. Nice hyperpop.

Powers and interactions:
- Four "command" buttons bottom: CREATE, DESTROY, CHANGE, EVERYTHING (or "ANYTHING"). Each with distinct effect:
  - CREATE: burst of glowing life orbs that spawn, orbit the goddess, then become little butterfly-like sprites/points; counter increases; sound arpeggio; text "LIFE, BORN FROM NOTHING".
  - DESTROY: shockwave ring expands, world desaturates/shakes, life orbs implode into the goddess hand, floor cracks (lines flash), screen glitch, text "ASHES. THEN SILENCE."
  - CHANGE: hue-shift entire palette (CSS var + uniforms + light colors) cycling through themes (bubblegum, acid, ice, void), goddess morphs scale/spin and material hue; text "FORM IS A SUGGESTION."
  - EVERYTHING: all at once — supernova, palette storm, many orbs, screen flash, big text "I AM EVERYTHING", maybe goddess grows and rings align.
- Keyboard shortcuts 1-4, space for everything. Touch buttons.
- Ambient audio via WebAudio: a soft pad chord with filtered saw, plus sparkle notes on actions. Start on first interaction, mute toggle. Should avoid autoplay issues. A "sound off" button; toggle. Not required but adds polish. Keep code robust.

UI:
- Top-left: small "HYPERDEITY" brand + "ALTAR 001" maybe.
- Title center-top or left: big display font "SHE / IS / EVERYTHING" with gradient text and glitch layers. Hyperpop: italic heavy sans, chrome gradient, outline. Use Google Fonts? Network may be unavailable in preview. Better embed fonts? System fonts fallback: "Arial Black", Impact, "Helvetica Neue". We could download a font (e.g., from Google Fonts) and vendor woff2. Check network. Use `curl` to fetch fonts. Let's see if network works.
- Power buttons: pill glassy chrome with gradient border, hover glow, icons.
- Status: "LIFE: 000" counter, theme name, hint "drag to orbit · scroll to zoom · 1–4 to command".
- Bottom mobile responsive: buttons in 2x2 grid, smaller title.

Accessibility: aria-labels, keyboard, reduced motion? Provide.

Loading: instant (no external assets), but add a brief intro overlay that fades. However capture auto-start only clicks "Start/Play" buttons. If we have an overlay with "ENTER" button, auto-start won't click it and screenshot will show overlay — bad. So no blocking intro. Auto-run immediately with an animated entrance. Avoid any button labeled exactly "start"/"play" to prevent capture auto-click. Our buttons are "CREATE LIFE" etc., not matching.

Performance: keep pixel ratio capped at 1.75, bloom at half res? UnrealBloom handles. Mobile: reduce particles and bloom. Use responsive.

Screenshot verification: use start.sh with PORT=3002? default-start listens PORT || 3000. README says Pascal dev server 3002 but here use 3000/3002. Start via `PORT=3002 RUNTIME_DIR=... ./start.sh` in background. Then playwright-cli open and screenshot. Then read the image.

Network works. Vendor three. Let's pick r170 or newer. Use npm? Simpler download build/three.module.js and addons from jsdelivr. But addons import "three" — importmap handles. Let's get:

- addons/postprocessing: EffectComposer, RenderPass, ShaderPass, MaskPass, UnrealBloomPass, OutputPass
- addons/shaders: CopyShader, LuminosityHighPassShader, OutputShader

Alternatively use importmap pointing to jsdelivr and rely on network — but preview may be offline? The runner has network; public preview users likely too, but self-contained is safer.

Fonts: download a hyperpop-ish display font. Google Fonts woff2 e.g. "Anton" (bold condensed) + "Space Grotesk" or "Archivo Black". Hyperpop often uses italic heavy. "Bricolage Grotesque"? Let's fetch from Google Fonts API CSS and woff2 files, vendor them. Use @font-face. E.g., "Archivo Black" (regular), "Space Grotesk" 400/700, and maybe "Unbounded" (hyperpop-ish). Unbounded is a great display font, geometric futuristic. Use Unbounded 700/900 for headings, Space Grotesk for body. Both on Google Fonts. Download woff2 (latin).

Let me fetch CSS with a modern UA to get woff2.

Now design details in code.

Structure:
- index.html with canvas + UI markup, importmap, main.js module.
- styles.css
- main.js (maybe split into modules: scene.js, figure.js, powers.js, audio.js, ui.js for maintainability). A few modules is fine.

Let's plan the figure carefully. Coordinates: figure root at y=0 (floor at y=0). Height ~3.2.

Use materials:
- chrome: MeshPhysicalMaterial({ color: 0xffe9ff, metalness: 1, roughness: 0.08, envMapIntensity: 1.8, clearcoat: 1, clearcoatRoughness: 0.1, iridescence: 1, iridescenceIOR: 1.6, iridescenceThicknessRange: [100, 700] }) — three supports iridescence.
- accent: emissive pink.
- gown: MeshPhysicalMaterial({ color: 0xff2fd0, transmission: .6, thickness: .5, roughness: .15, metalness: .4, transparent: true, opacity: .85, iridescence: 1, side: DoubleSide }) maybe transmission needs renderer transmission pass — works.
- hair: MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x120016, metalness: .8, roughness: .25, emissive: 0x2a0033 }).

Body via lathe:
torso profile points (x radius, y height):
y from 0.95 (hip top) to 2.05 (shoulders):
- (0.34, 1.0) hips
- (0.36, 1.15)
- (0.30, 1.35) waist
- (0.33, 1.55) ribcage
- (0.37, 1.75) bust line
- (0.32, 1.9)
- (0.20, 2.02) shoulder base
- (0.09, 2.08) neck base
Lathe with 48 segments. Add scale z 0.72 to flatten front-back (scale group z). Actually lathe circular cross-section; scale z .75 gives elliptical body.

Bust: two spheres at y=1.72, x ±0.14, z 0.20, radius .14 scaled (1, .9, .8). Subtle, chrome.
Pelvis: sphere at y=0.95 radius .34 scaled (1, .8, .8), maybe merge look. Hips.
Neck: cylinder y 2.08-2.22 radius .08.
Head: sphere y=2.38 radius .19 scaled (0.85,1.1,0.9). Face direction +z. Add jaw/chin small sphere? Use a custom lathe head? Sphere with slight scaling is fine stylized.
Eyes: two glowing capsules at y=2.39, x ±0.065, z 0.155, small spheres radius .018, emissive magenta intensity high. Add eyebrow accents? no.
Hair: cap sphere behind head (slightly larger, dark), plus ~14 long strands using CatmullRomCurve3 flowing outward/down with curls, TubeGeometry radius .02-.045. Strands start around head and flow outward to sides and down to ~1.2, as if floating. Add some pink emissive thin strands among them. Hair cap: sphere r .205 scaled, position z -.02, using phi range? Use full sphere slightly bigger and cut? A sphere will cover face. Use SphereGeometry with thetaStart etc. Simpler: hair cap as sphere at z=-0.05, scaled (1.0,1.05,0.85), so it doesn't cover face front (face at z +0.15). Head front z .17; cap extends to z=-0.05+0.16=0.11, so face visible. Add fringe strands over forehead.

Arms: right arm raised: shoulder at (0.34, 2.0, 0), upper arm to elbow (0.62, 2.28, 0.05), forearm to hand (0.78, 2.62, 0.18), palm up orb at (0.8, 2.78, 0.2). Build with capsules/cylinders oriented between points via helper. Left arm down/out: shoulder (-0.34,2.0), elbow (-0.5,1.6,0.06), hand (-0.42,1.2,0.18) holding a floating shard? Maybe palm facing up with tiny galaxy.
Hands: small spheres scaled.

Legs: from hip (±0.14, 0.95) to knee (±0.16, 0.5) to ankle (±0.14, 0.12). Since gown covers, add slim chrome legs visible through slit. Feet: small elongated spheres/boxes at y .06, z .08, high heels. Gown: flowing translucent skirt from hips y .98 down to .15, flaring to radius .7 at bottom with wavy hem. Build custom BufferGeometry with 64 radial segments and 12 vertical rings, radius r(t) = .33 + .5*t^1.3 with wave sin(6θ + phase)*.05*t, and vertical y = .98 - .83*t + wave. Double side, iridescent. Add slit by varying? Could just be translucent so legs show through. Add vertical flowing ribbon panels around for ethereal movement.
Also shoulder pauldrons? Chrome shards floating above shoulders, crown floating above head: 5 tapered shards arranged in a tiara arc, emissive edges.

Halo: torus behind head radius .45, tube .012, emissive gradient via vertex colors? Use MeshBasicMaterial pink + additive glow + bloom. Second torus larger rotated. Also orbiting rings around body (radius 1.3, tilted) with small gems.

The figure should be the hero, centered. Camera at (0, 2.2, 6.2), lookAt (0,1.7,0). Auto orbit slight ±0.25 rad. On desktop title at left might overlap? Put title top-left and figure centered/right? Better composition: figure center-right, title left. But on mobile, title top, figure center. We can offset camera target x? Simpler: title top-left over scene with gradient scrim, figure centered. Big title can overlap upper left but figure's head at center. Keep title max-width 40vw, font-size clamp; on mobile top center smaller.

Alternatively title bottom-left big "SHE IS EVERYTHING" with powers bottom center/right. Hmm. Hyperpop poster: huge type behind figure (3D text?) — Use HTML giant outlined text behind? The canvas is behind UI, so text overlays. Could place a giant vertical word "GODDESS" as background with mix-blend-mode overlay at low opacity. Nice.

Let's design UI:
- Top bar: left brand "♱ HYPERDEITY" / "ALTAR_001"; right: sound toggle, "REALM: BUBBLEGUM" pill.
- Left middle: eyebrow "SHE CAN DO ANYTHING", h1 "EVERYTHING" huge chrome gradient italic? plus subtitle "A hyperpop deity simulator. Command her. She will obey — or not."
- Counter: "SOULS IN ORBIT 000" near bottom left, plus hint.
- Bottom center: power dock with 4 buttons each with icon glyph, label, key hint. On desktop horizontal, mobile 2x2.
- Center bottom floating caption for action results, big kinetic text ("LIFE, BORN FROM NOTHING"), fades.
- Cursor glow? CSS radial follow.

Colors via CSS vars updated by theme:
themes:
1. BUBBLEGUM: bg #12001a, pink #ff2fd0, cyan #47f9ff, violet #8a2bff, accent #ff8ae2.
2. ACID: bg #071000, lime #c6ff00, cyan #00ffd0, magenta #ff00a8.
3. ICE: bg #020814, cyan #66e0ff, white, violet.
4. INFERNO: bg #140000, orange #ff5a1f, pink, gold.
Change cycles. Update CSS vars, scene lights, ring colors, particle colors, bloom? Use uniforms.

Implement scene update with time. Interaction state machine:
- `power(kind)` sets state timers.
- Life orbs: maintain array of life objects each a small sprite/mesh with orbit params, spawned in bursts; max ~60. Each is a glowing sphere with sprite halo? Use Points with custom shader for efficiency? Simpler InstancedMesh spheres with emissive material and additive sprites. 60 draw calls fine but sprite halos 60 more. Use a single Points cloud for "souls" with attributes color/size and update positions per frame. Great: PointsMaterial with map = radial gradient texture, vertexColors, additive, depthWrite false. Update positions from orbit params. Spawn animation scale via alpha? PointsMaterial size global; use custom shader for per-point size/alpha. Let's write ShaderMaterial for souls: attributes position, aColor, aSize, aPhase; vertex sets gl_PointSize = aSize * (300/-mvPosition.z); fragment radial glow. Uniform uTime, uOpacity. Nice.
- On create: add N souls with random orbits around goddess (radius 1.2-3.0, y 0.4-3.4), plus a burst ring effect at hand. Counter updates.
- On destroy: souls implode (set target radius 0 and remove after 1s with shrink), shockwave mesh expands, screen shake, glitch class on body for 600ms, floor cracks flash. Maybe leave 0.
- On change: palette transition (lerp colors over .8s), goddess spin + scale pulse, ring rotation speed changes, text.
- On everything: create 30 souls, supernova flash (CSS white overlay), huge shockwave, palette random, camera pull back/zoom pulse, goddess arms flare? Screen shake; text "I AM EVERYTHING". Maybe temporarily show many "eyes" on figure? Keep.

Goddess idle animation: floating bob (sin), hair strands sway via updating geometry? Updating TubeGeometry each frame is costly. Instead animate strand groups' rotation slightly and scale; or build hair as skinned? Simpler: each strand is a mesh in a group with pivot at head; rotate subtly with sin offsets, giving float. Gown waves via vertex shader: custom onBeforeCompile or ShaderMaterial. Use a ShaderMaterial for gown with gradient + fresnel + vertex displacement waves (sin(time + y*... + angle)). Gown should look iridescent; custom shader with fresnel rainbow. That's gorgeous and cheap. Similarly halo shader.

Floor: circle plane radius 14 with shader: radial fade, concentric rings, grid, reflection fake (vertical gradient mirrored?). Use MeshPhysicalMaterial for real reflection? Without envmap reflections of goddess. Could use Reflector addon (mirror) — adds render pass cost, but a chrome floor reflecting the goddess would be stunning. Three addons/objects/Reflector.js. Use a dark reflective floor with Reflector at y=0, opacity? Reflector material can be customized; use `Reflector` with textureWidth 1024, color 0x1a001f, and overlay a grid plane above with additive transparency. That doubles render cost but scene is simple. On mobile reduce reflector resolution or skip (fallback standard material). The reflection of neon figure on black glass floor = premium. Let's use Reflector with clipBias, color tinted dark, then add circular platform edge glow.

Wait: Reflector renders scene from mirrored camera; the figure's gown transparent etc. Fine.

Add fog for depth: scene.fog = FogExp2(bg, 0.035).

Environment: PMREM from RoomEnvironment gives white studio reflections. Tint by adding colored lights. For hyperpop chrome, reflections should include pink/cyan. Build custom env scene: black room with emissive panels: large pink plane on left, cyan on right, white strip top, magenta behind. PMREMGenerator.fromScene(envScene, 0.04). This creates colorful chrome. Great.

Lights: key spot pink from front-left, rim cyan from behind-right, fill violet, point light in hand (magenta). Ambient low.

Post: EffectComposer + RenderPass + UnrealBloomPass + custom ShaderPass final (vignette, grain, chromatic aberration, slight scanline) + OutputPass. Order: RenderPass -> Bloom -> OutputPass -> FinalGrade? OutputPass does tone mapping and color space; a custom pass after OutputPass works in sRGB. Fine. Set renderer.toneMapping = ACESFilmic, exposure 1.1; OutputPass handles.

Custom final shader: uv distortion from uShake? Chromatic aberration sampled on tDiffuse with offsets; vignette; grain (hash with uTime); subtle horizontal scanline; `uGlitch` uniform increases RGB split and block displacement. Screen flash handled by CSS overlay or uniform. Use CSS overlay for flash simpler.

Camera: perspective 45, position (0, 2.1, 6.4). Drag orbit: yaw/pitch around target; wheel zoom 4.5–9. Auto rotation when idle. Touch: pointer events; single finger drag orbits; pinch zoom maybe implement. Prevent page scroll with touch-action none on canvas.

Intro: figure rises from floor with opacity? Materials transparent initially? Simpler camera dolly from 9 to 6.4 over 2.4s with ease, rings spin up. No overlay.

Audio: WebAudio synth pad. On first pointerdown/keydown, create AudioContext, start 3-osc pad (detuned saw through lowpass + gain .04), plus slow LFO. Actions: sparkle arpeggio (sine pings with decay), destroy (noise burst + low sine drop), change (filter sweep), everything (chord swell). Add sound toggle default on but suspended until gesture; UI shows "SOUND: TAP TO WAKE"? Better default muted icon and start after first interaction with `audio.start()`; show a small "SOUND ON/OFF" toggle. Ensure no console errors if AudioContext not allowed. Keep robust.

Text captions: central bottom-ish big kinetic text with CSS animation. Also command history ticker? Maybe a "log" of goddess quotes in corner: random phrases on actions. Nice narrative:
- create: "LET THERE BE / LIGHT" or "LIFE, BORN FROM NOTHING"
- destroy: "ASHES. THEN SILENCE." / "I UNMAKE IT ALL"
- change: "FORM IS A SUGGESTION" / "BECOME OTHERWISE"
- everything: "I AM EVERYTHING" / "ALL AT ONCE. ALWAYS."
Cycle random.

Counter "LIVES CREATED" increments.

Also add a small instruction "DRAG TO ORBIT · SCROLL TO ZOOM · 1-4 COMMAND".

Code architecture:
- index.html: importmap, canvas container, UI.
- styles.css
- src/main.js: init scene, figure, powers, audio, UI wiring.
- src/figure.js: createGoddess(env) returns group + refs (gown, hairStrands, halo, rings, handOrb, eyes).

- src/powers.js? Could keep interactions in main.

Use npm pack or curl from jsdelivr. Let's fetch and recursively resolve imports. I'll just fetch known files:

- examples/jsm/postprocessing/{EffectComposer,RenderPass,ShaderPass,MaskPass,UnrealBloomPass,OutputPass}.js
- examples/jsm/shaders/{CopyShader,LuminosityHighPassShader,OutputShader}.js

## ✦ HYPERDEITY — She Can Do Anything

A playable 3D hyperpop altar. A chrome goddess floats above a mirrored stage,
wearing a crown of shards and a holographic gown. Command her and the world
changes around her.

### Powers

| Command | Key | What happens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Create Life** | `1` | Souls are born in her hand and take up orbit around the altar. |
| **Destroy** | `2` | Every soul implodes, the camera shakes, the world glitches, and the light drains out. |
| **Change** | `3` | Reality recompiles into a new palette: Bubblegum, Acid Bloom, Cryo Dream, or Solar Flare. |
| **Everything** | `4` / `Space` | All of it at once: a supernova, a new realm, and a screen-wide revelation. |

### Controls

- **Drag** to orbit the altar, **scroll / pinch** to zoom.
- **1–4** or **Space** on a keyboard.
- **Sound** starts on the first command and can be toggled from the top bar.

### Tech

- Three.js `r170`, vendored locally so the experience runs without a network.
- Custom chrome / iridescent goddess built from lathed and extruded geometry.
- Mirrored floor, orbital rings, floating Y2K trinkets, soul particles, shockwaves,
  sparks, bloom, film grain, chromatic aberration, and a glitch grade.
- Web Audio ambient pad and synthesized sound design.
- Responsive from 390 px phones to widescreen desktops, with touch and safe-area support.

The static site is served from the repository root; no build step is required.

## Objective
- Build an interactive 3D hyperpop experience for a female God who can do anything: create life, destroy, change reality, and do everything at once, based on the user's request "a female God where she can do ANYTHING ... EVERTHING she can create life destroy change ... do many things 3D hyperpop".

## Requirements
- 3D hyperpop aesthetic.
- Female deity character.
- Powers: create life, destroy, change, and "everything".
- Must run as a static browser app via the existing OMGithub runtime.

## Decisions
- Built with Three.js r170, vendored locally under `vendor/three/` so the experience works offline.
- Procedural chrome goddess rather than an external model, allowing animated hair/gown/crown and full palette control.
- Four powers with distinct effects, keyboard shortcuts 1–4/Space, and sound synthesized with Web Audio.
- Responsive layout for desktop 1440×900 and mobile 390×844; touch orbit/pinch controls.
- Mobile uses a glossy floor instead of the Reflector mirror for performance; desktop keeps the mirrored floor.
- Verified with Playwright screenshots; SwiftShader is CPU software rendering and measures roughly 4–10 FPS, so visual quality was prioritized over software-render performance.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built full static app: `index.html`, `styles.css`, `src/main.js`, `src/environment.js`, `src/figure.js`, `src/effects.js`, `src/audio.js`.
- Implemented chrome goddess with crown, halo, long hair, gown, face details, chest gem, orb, chrome hearts/stars, orbital rings, mirrored floor, grid/dais, particles.
- Implemented Create/Destroy/Change/Everything powers with soul particles, bursts, shockwaves, palette themes, glitch, screen flash, erase dim, camera shake, captions, and synthesized audio.
- Added responsive UI: title, ticker, stats, realm chip, sound toggle, power dock, mobile hint, safe-area handling.
- Vendored Three.js addons and Unbounded/Space Grotesk fonts.
- Added favicon and README documentation.
- Verified desktop, tablet, and mobile screenshots; no JS errors, only WebGL performance warnings.
- Final screenshot generated at `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/desktop-face.png`.
